Its settings install the four middleware, require HTTPS, and set a content security policy whose scripts must come from the site itself or carry the request's nonce (`django/utils/csp.py:CSP`):

The headers came in the order the middleware added them, which is the onion read from the inside; a response keeps its cookies apart, and the handler writes them after its headers (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIHandler.__call__`).

Last, `SecurityMiddleware` added Strict-Transport-Security, which it sends only on a secure request, and three headers whose settings are on by default (`django/middleware/security.py:SecurityMiddleware.process_response`).

A second request from the same client got the same secret back in its cookie and a different token in its page, since every call of `get_token` makes a new mask (`django/middleware/csrf.py:get_token`).

`SecurityMiddleware.process_request` answered with a redirect to the same address over HTTPS, so the three middleware inside it never ran and the redirect carried none of their headers; it still had `SecurityMiddleware`'s own, added as its response went out (`django/middleware/security.py:SecurityMiddleware.process_request`):

A template that writes `{% csrf_token %}` calls `get_token` by way of the CSRF context processor, which makes a secret if the request had none and marks it to be sent back; on the way out, `CsrfViewMiddleware.process_response` sets the cookie, or stores the secret in the session ([The CSRF secret and its token](security/csrf-token.md)) (`django/middleware/csrf.py:CsrfViewMiddleware.process_response`).

A request that fails is answered by the view `CSRF_FAILURE_VIEW` names, `csrf_failure` by default, with a 403, and the view it was going to is never called ([The CSRF check: `CsrfViewMiddleware.process_view`](security/csrf-check.md)) (`django/middleware/csrf.py:CsrfViewMiddleware.process_view`).
The token is masked so that it differs on every page while the secret stays the same; Django's documentation gives the reason as protection against the BREACH attack (`docs/ref/csrf.txt`).

The secret is kept from request to request; `rotate_token`, which `login` in `django.contrib.auth` calls, replaces it, as does `CsrfViewMiddleware.process_request` itself when a request's cookie is malformed (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:login`, `django/middleware/csrf.py:rotate_token`).

A view can also change what the middleware do for it alone: `xframe_options_exempt` marks its response to be left without X-Frame-Options, and `csp_override` gives its response a policy of its own, which the middleware then uses in place of `SECURE_CSP` (`django/views/decorators/clickjacking.py:xframe_options_exempt`, `django/views/decorators/csp.py:csp_override`).

On the way out, `build_policy` writes the policy from the setting's dictionary, and replaces the placeholder `CSP.NONCE` with the nonce if the nonce was made, or drops it if not ([Content Security Policy: `ContentSecurityPolicyMiddleware` and the nonce](security/csp.md)) (`django/utils/csp.py:build_policy`).

The base of them is `salted_hmac`, which makes an HMAC of a value with a key made by hashing a salt, which names the use, together with the secret key; so each use has a key of its own, and a value made for one use does not verify for another ([Secret keys and `django.utils.crypto`](security/keys.md)) (`django/utils/crypto.py:salted_hmac`).

`dumps` signs any value that JSON can hold, by way of a `TimestampSigner` with the salt `"django.core.signing"` unless it is given another, and `loads` checks it and gives the value back ([Signing: `Signer`, `TimestampSigner`, `dumps` and `loads`](security/signing.md)) (`django/core/signing.py:dumps`):
A `Signer` tries its key and then each of the fallbacks, which is how a site changes its key without at once losing every value signed with the old one (`django/core/signing.py:Signer.unsign`).

The security checks are system checks with the tag `"security"`, and most are registered as deployment checks, which run only when the check command is given `--deploy`: that `settings.DEBUG` is off, that `SECRET_KEY` is long and not one startproject wrote, that `SecurityMiddleware`, `CsrfViewMiddleware` and `XFrameOptionsMiddleware` are installed and the cookies marked secure ([The security checks](security/checks.md)) ([The system checks](commands/checks.md)) (`django/core/checks/security/base.py:check_secret_key`).

Three run on every check: that the two policy settings are dictionaries, that a policy with a nonce has the `csp` context processor to put the nonce in templates, and that the view `CSRF_FAILURE_VIEW` names takes a request and a reason (`django/core/checks/security/csrf.py:check_csrf_failure_view`).

Two of the checks they rely on are the request's: `HttpRequest.get_host`, which ordinarily refuses a host not in `ALLOWED_HOSTS`, and `HttpRequest.is_secure`, which a proxy's header can decide ([Headers, host and scheme](http/headers.md)); and checking a URL before redirecting to it is in [The helpers in `django/utils/http.py`](http/helpers.md).
